records.source: ה֣וֹי הַיֹּרְדִ֤ים מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לְעֶזְרָ֔ה עַל־סוּסִ֖ים יִשָּׁעֵ֑נוּ וַיִּבְטְח֨וּ עַל־רֶ֜כֶב כִּ֣י רָ֗ב וְעַ֤ל פָּֽרָשִׁים֙ כִּֽי־עָצְמ֣וּ מְאֹ֔ד וְלֹ֤א שָׁעוּ֙ עַל־קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֶת־יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א דָרָֽשׁוּ׃
records.gloss: Woe, [those] going down [to] Egypt for help; on horses they lean, and they trust in chariotry because [it is] many, and in horsemen because they are strong exceedingly, and not they look to [the] Holy One of Israel, and Yahweh not they seek.
pieces: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help! \q They lean on horses; \q they put their confidence in chariots, for there are many of them, and in cavalry, for it is very strong. \q But they do not turn their eyes to the Holy One of Israel; \q they do not inquire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.1: Woe, those who go down to Egypt for help, [who] lean on horses \q and trust in chariots because [they are] many, and in horsemen because they are very strong, \q but they do not look to the Holy One of Israel, \q and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they do not seek!

R.1: How terrible it will be for those who go down to Egypt for help! They depend on horses. \q They trust in Egypt's many chariots and its strong soldiers on horseback. \q But they never look to the Holy One of Israel. Nor do they ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help.

decisions.choice: going down to Egypt for help: Judah's leaders seeking an alliance with Egypt against Assyria
decisions.reason: In Hezekiah's reign Judah's rulers looked to Egypt for military support against Assyria. Chapter 30 condemns the same embassy (30:1-7), and the Assyrian officer later mocks that trust (36:6, 9). Egypt lay to the south and lower, so travelers "went down" to it.

decisions.choice: horses, chariots and horsemen: the military power God's people were told not to rely on
decisions.reason: The law forbade a king to gather many horses or to send the people back to Egypt for them (Deuteronomy 17:16), and the psalms set trust in chariots and horses against trust in the LORD (Psalm 20:8; 33:17). The verse uses the same verb for trusting that 30:12 and 36:4-9 use.

decisions.choice: seek the LORD: ask the LORD for guidance, consult him
decisions.reason: The verb is used for asking God's will, often through a prophet (8:19; 30:2, where they did not ask God's mouth). The leaders made their plans without consulting him.

decisions.choice: Egypt's many chariots and its strong soldiers on horseback
decisions.reason: Readable says whose chariots and horsemen these are; the context is Egypt's army.

records.heading: Horses from Egypt or the Holy One of Israel

records.source: וְגַם־ה֤וּא חָכָם֙ וַיָּ֣בֵא רָ֔ע וְאֶת־דְּבָרָ֖יו לֹ֣א הֵסִ֑יר וְקָם֙ עַל־בֵּ֣ית מְרֵעִ֔ים וְעַל־עֶזְרַ֖ת פֹּ֥עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
records.gloss: And also he [is] wise, and he brings disaster, and his words not he turns aside; and he will rise against [the] house of evildoers and against [the] help of workers of wickedness.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is wise as well: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings disaster and does not withdraw what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has said. \q He will rise up against the house of evildoers \q and against those who come to the aid of wrongdoers.

L.2: Yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also [is] wise, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings disaster, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not call back; \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rise up against the house of evildoers \q and against the help of the workers of wickedness.

R.2: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is wise too. He brings disaster, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not take back what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has said. \q He will rise up against those evil people and against everyone who comes to help them.

decisions.choice: he too is wise: an ironic answer to the planners who trust their own wisdom
decisions.reason: Judah's counselors thought their Egyptian plan was clever (29:14-15; 30:1-2). The prophet answers that the LORD is wise too, and his word of judgment will stand (40:8; 55:11).

decisions.choice: the house of evildoers and the help of wrongdoers: those in Judah who turned to Egypt, and Egypt who helped them
alternatives: Egypt as the house of evildoers
decisions.reason: Verse 3 names the two parties as "the helper" and "the one helped". The evildoers are most likely the rebellious leaders of Judah (30:1, 9), and their help is Egypt (30:5-7). Some take the house of evildoers to be Egypt itself.

decisions.choice: the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, the LORD of verse 1, so the reader knows who "he" is.

records.source: וּמִצְרַ֤יִם אָדָם֙ וְֽלֹא־אֵ֔ל וְסוּסֵיהֶ֥ם בָּשָׂ֖ר וְלֹא־ר֑וּחַ וַֽיהוָ֞ה יַטֶּ֣ה יָד֗וֹ וְכָשַׁ֤ל עוֹזֵר֙ וְנָפַ֣ל עָזֻ֔ר וְיַחְדָּ֖ו כֻּלָּ֥ם יִכְלָיֽוּן׃ס
records.gloss: And Egypt [is] human and not God, and their horses flesh and not spirit; and Yahweh will stretch out his hand, and will stumble [the one who] helps, and will fall [the one who is] helped, and together all of them will come to an end.
pieces: Egypt is human and not God; \q its horses are flesh and not spirit. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will stretch out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand: the one who gives help will stagger, the one who receives it will go down, \q and both will be finished together.

L.3: And Egypt [is] human and not God, \q and their horses [are] flesh and not spirit; \q and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will stretch out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, and the helper will stumble, and the helped will fall, \q and they will all come to an end together.

R.3: The Egyptians are only human. They are not God. \q Their horses are only flesh and blood. They are not spirit. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will reach out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand to strike. Then Egypt, the helper, will trip, and Judah, the one it helped, will fall. \q They will all be destroyed together.

decisions.choice: human, not God; flesh, not spirit: the weakness of every created power set against God's power
decisions.reason: "Flesh" is what is mortal and frail; "spirit" is the life and strength that come from God (Genesis 6:3; 40:6-8). Egypt's army, however large, belongs to the first kind.

decisions.choice: stretch out his hand: act in judgment
decisions.reason: The phrase is used for the LORD striking a people (5:25; 14:26-27; 23:11). Here one blow brings down both Egypt and those who trusted it.

decisions.choice: the helper and the one helped: Egypt and Judah
decisions.reason: The two participles pick up the "help" of verses 1-2. Egypt is the helper; the leaders of Judah who went to it are the ones helped (30:5-7).

decisions.choice: to strike; Egypt, the helper; Judah, the one it helped
decisions.reason: Readable says what the outstretched hand does and names the helper and the one helped (see m3).

records.source: כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר־יְהוָ֣ה׀אֵלַ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶהְגֶּה֩ הָאַרְיֵ֨ה וְהַכְּפִ֜יר עַל־טַרְפּ֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִקָּרֵ֤א עָלָיו֙ מְלֹ֣א רֹעִ֔ים מִקּוֹלָם֙ לֹ֣א יֵחָ֔ת וּמֵֽהֲמוֹנָ֖ם לֹ֣א יַֽעֲנֶ֑ה כֵּ֗ן יֵרֵד֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת לִצְבֹּ֥א עַל־הַר־צִיּ֖וֹן וְעַל־גִּבְעָתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: For thus has said Yahweh to me: As growls the lion, and the young lion, over its prey, when is called against it a multitude of shepherds, from their voice not it is terrified, and from their noise not it cowers, so will come down Yahweh of hosts to wage war on Mount Zion and on its hill.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said this to me: Think of a lion, a young lion, rumbling over its kill. A crowd of shepherds is called out against it, \q yet their yelling does not scare it \q and their uproar does not make it shrink back. \q In the same way {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies will come down to wage war on Mount Zion and on its hill.

L.4: For thus {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said to me: As the lion growls, the young lion, over its prey, when a band of shepherds is called out against it, \q [and] it is not terrified by their voice \q and does not cower at their noise, \q so {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts will come down \q to wage war on Mount Zion and on its hill.

R.4: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told me: A lion may growl over the animal it has killed. Even if a crowd of shepherds comes out against it, \q it is not afraid of their shouts. \q Their noise does not make it run away. \q In the same way, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies will come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its hill.

decisions.choice: to wage war on Mount Zion: the preposition can mean "against" or "upon"; the sense is left open
decisions.reason: With this verb the preposition often means "against" (29:7-8; Numbers 31:7), and the lion growling over its prey could picture the LORD as Zion's attacker. But the prey is his own, and no one can take it from him; verse 5 then speaks of him shielding Jerusalem. Most likely the LORD comes down to fight on Zion for its defense, but the wording keeps the tension.

decisions.choice: a band of shepherds called out: herdsmen gathering to drive a lion from the flock
decisions.reason: Shepherds defended their flocks from lions (1 Samuel 17:34-35; Amos 3:12). A grown lion that has made its kill is not frightened off by their shouting.

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} comes down to Mount Zion

records.source: כְּצִפֳּרִ֣ים עָפ֔וֹת כֵּ֗ן יָגֵ֛ן יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת עַל־יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם גָּנ֥וֹן וְהִצִּ֖יל פָּסֹ֥חַ וְהִמְלִֽיט׃
records.gloss: Like birds flying, so will shield Yahweh of hosts over Jerusalem, shielding and delivering, passing over and rescuing.
pieces: Like birds on the wing, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies will protect Jerusalem: \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will protect and rescue, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will pass over and deliver.

L.5: Like birds hovering, \q so {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts will shield over Jerusalem, \q shielding and delivering, passing over and rescuing.

R.5: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies will protect Jerusalem the way birds fly over their nests to protect their young. \q He will guard the city and rescue it. He will pass over it and save it.

decisions.choice: pass over: spare, as at the first Passover
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in Exodus 12:13, 23, 27, where the LORD passed over the houses of Israel and spared them. It is used only there and here in this sense, so the picture is of a new Passover rescue.

decisions.choice: shielding, delivering, passing over, rescuing: four emphatic verb forms
decisions.reason: The four verbs are infinitive forms that stress the certainty of the action. The rescue is told in 37:33-36, when the Assyrian army failed to take Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the way birds fly over their nests to protect their young
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture of birds hovering protectively. The nest and the young are implied, not stated.

records.source: שׁ֗וּבוּ לַאֲשֶׁ֛ר הֶעְמִ֥יקוּ סָרָ֖ה בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Return to [the one against] whom they have made deep revolt, O sons of Israel.
pieces: Turn back, {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, to the one from whom they have gone so deep into rebellion.

L.6: Return to [the one against] whom they have made revolt deep, O {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.6: Come back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}! You have rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} so deeply.

decisions.choice: they have rebelled ... O sons of Israel: a shift between speaking to the people and about them
decisions.reason: The call is addressed to Israel, but the clause describing the rebellion speaks of "them". Hebrew poetry often moves between second and third person in this way; those addressed are the rebels themselves.

decisions.choice: made revolt deep: rebelled deeply and deliberately
decisions.reason: "Making deep" is used for sin that is serious and hidden (29:15; Hosea 9:9).

decisions.choice: the LORD; You have rebelled
decisions.reason: Readable names the one Israel is called back to and speaks of the rebellion as "you", since those addressed are the rebels (see m1).

records.source: כִּ֚י בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִמְאָס֗וּן אִ֚ישׁ אֱלִילֵ֣י כַסְפּ֔וֹ וֶאֱלִילֵ֖י זְהָב֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֥וּ לָכֶ֛ם יְדֵיכֶ֖ם חֵֽטְא׃
records.gloss: For in day the that they will reject, each [one], his idols of silver and his idols of gold, which have made for you your hands, sin.
pieces: For on that day each of them will spurn their idols of silver and their idols of gold, \q the sin your own hands have made for you.

L.7: For in that day they will reject, each [one], his idols of silver and his idols of gold, \q which your hands have made for you, [as] sin.

R.7: At that time all of them will throw away their idols of silver and gold. \q You made those idols with your own hands, and that was a sin.

decisions.choice: sin: the idols themselves are called a sin
decisions.reason: The last word stands alone at the end. It describes the idols as a sin made by their hands; it could also be read as "your sinful hands".

decisions.choice: throwing away idols of silver and gold: the turning that will come when the LORD acts
decisions.reason: The same picture is in 2:20 and 30:22. Turning to the LORD (verse 6) means giving up the gods they had made.

records.source: וְנָפַ֤ל אַשּׁוּר֙ בְּחֶ֣רֶב לֹא־אִ֔ישׁ וְחֶ֥רֶב לֹֽא־אָדָ֖ם תֹּֽאכֲלֶ֑נּוּ וְנָ֥ס לוֹ֙ מִפְּנֵי־חֶ֔רֶב וּבַחוּרָ֖יו לָמַ֥ס יִהְיֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And will fall Assyria by a sword not of a man, and a sword not of a human will devour it; and it will flee for itself from before a sword, and its young men for forced labor will become.
pieces: Assyria will fall by a sword that no man wields; \q a sword that is not human will devour it. \q It will run from the sword, \q and its young men will be put to forced labor.

L.8: And Assyria will fall by a sword not of a man, \q and a sword not of a human will devour it; \q and it will flee from before a sword, \q and its young men will become forced labor.

R.8: Assyria will be struck down, but not by any human weapon. A sword that no person holds will destroy it. \q Its people will run from that sword. \q Its young men will be made to do forced labor.

decisions.choice: a sword not of a man: Assyria will be defeated by God himself, not by a human army
decisions.reason: The account of 37:36 tells how the angel of the LORD struck the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib returned home. The same pattern of God acting without human strength is in 10:33-34 and 30:31.

decisions.choice: forced labor: conscripted work for a conqueror
decisions.reason: The word is used for peoples made to do labor gangs for another nation (Judges 1:28; 1 Kings 9:21). Assyria, which enslaved others, will be humbled the same way.

records.source: וְסַלְעוֹ֙ מִמָּג֣וֹר יַֽעֲב֔וֹר וְחַתּ֥וּ מִנֵּ֖ס שָׂרָ֑יו נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁר־א֥וּר לוֹ֙ בְּצִיּ֔וֹן וְתַנּ֥וּר ל֖וֹ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And its rock from terror will pass away, and will be dismayed from [the] standard its commanders, declares Yahweh, who [has] a fire in Zion and a furnace in Jerusalem.
pieces: Its rock will give way in terror, \q its officers will be shaken at the sight of the signal flag, \q declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who keeps a fire in Zion \q and a furnace in Jerusalem.

L.9: And its rock will pass away from terror, \q and its commanders will be dismayed at the signal flag, \q declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who has a fire in Zion \q and a furnace in Jerusalem.

R.9: Their mighty leader will run away in terror. \q Their commanders will panic when they see the signal flag. \q That is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says. His fire burns in Zion, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} furnace is in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: its rock: Assyria's king, or the stronghold it relied on
decisions.reason: "Rock" is a title for what gives safety (17:10; Deuteronomy 32:31, where it is used of other nations' gods). Here it most likely means the king, who fled home (37:37), but it may be the army's strength or fortress.

decisions.choice: at the signal flag: terrified at the sight of a raised standard
decisions.reason: The flag may be the signal the LORD raises (5:26; 18:3), or Assyria's own standard, which its officers desert in panic.

decisions.choice: a fire in Zion and a furnace in Jerusalem: the LORD's presence in his city, which consumes his enemies
decisions.reason: The altar fire burned at the temple, and the LORD is pictured as a fire that burns up those who oppose him (10:17; 29:6; 30:33).

decisions.choice: Their mighty leader
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the rock as the king (see m1).
